aiAgents.architecture: An agent is a controlled loop: retrieve context, choose a tool, act, record what happened, and stop when a rule says so. The model is one component next to APIs, permissions, evaluations and logs.
aiAgents.security: Tool access is scoped. Sensitive actions can require a person. Secrets stay out of prompts. We design for the least privilege the workflow needs.
aiAgents.eval: We define what “good” means for the workflow, test against real examples, and keep traces so failures are diagnosable after launch.
aiAgents.delivery: Assessment of systems and risk, a narrow pilot on one workflow, then production hardening: monitoring, permissions, runbooks and iteration.

faq.a: No. The useful pattern is an agent that does repetitive, well-specified work and escalates the rest.
Chat can be the interface. The product is the workflow: tools, data, permissions and the audit trail.

faq.q: What if our data is messy?
faq.a: Then the first job is often retrieval quality and process design.

softwarePage.approach: We map users, data and the systems you already pay for before we draw screens. Scope is a written slice, not an open-ended rebuild. The first release should be usable in production, even if it is narrow.
softwarePage.quality: We pick a stack your team can operate, usually TypeScript and React on the client and the backend that fits the rest of the estate. Tests, environments and a handover are part of the work, not a zip of source at the end.
softwarePage.delivery: Technical assessment of the current process, a first production-shaped release, then hardening: monitoring, access, documentation and a path to iterate.

faq.q: Do you only build greenfield products?
faq.a: No. Most engagements sit next to an existing process or system. We say what we will replace and what we will leave alone.

faq.q: Will we be locked into your stack?
faq.a: The contract is the system, not a framework fashion. We choose tools the people who will operate it can live with.
With the users, the data and the constraint. We do not start with a page of screens until those are clear.

softwarePage.ctaTitle: Have a process that deserves a real product?

dataPage.approach: A pipeline or a model is a production system. We define the decision it supports, the source of truth, who can see the output and what happens when it is wrong. We do not ship a notebook and call it done.
dataPage.quality: Checks on freshness and shape, documented ownership, and credentials that stay out of notebooks. If a number moves, someone should be able to trace it.
dataPage.delivery: Assessment of sources and the first decision worth automating, a narrow pipeline or model in production, then monitoring, access review and iteration.

faq.q: Do we need a data team first?
faq.a: You need an owner and a decision. We can start with one pipeline or one model. A platform for its own sake is usually the wrong first step.

faq.q: Will you train a model on day one?
faq.a: Only if a simpler rule or a better report will not do the job. The first work is often quality of the data and the process.

faq.q: How is this different from AI Agents?
faq.a: This pillar is data, models and infrastructure. Agents that call tools inside a workflow live on the AI Agents offering.

dataPage.ctaTitle: Have a number or a model that has to be trustworthy?
dataPage.ctaBody: Tell us the source, the decision and who gets blamed when it is wrong. We will tell you if a pipeline or a model is the right next step.

work.title: API integrations
work.body: Stable connections between the tools you already run, with retries, mapping and an owner when a field changes.

work.title: CRM and ERP links
work.body: The records sales, finance and operations already depend on, written once and kept consistent.

work.title: Workflow modernization
work.body: Replace the brittle manual path first. We do not rip out a working system to prove a point.

work.title: Automation you can see
work.body: Scheduled and event-driven jobs with logs operators can read, not a hidden script on someone's laptop.

work.title: Devices when they matter

integrationsPage.approach: We start with the copy-paste and the failure you cannot afford. Then we map which system is the source of truth for each field. The first integration should remove a daily tax, not announce a platform.
integrationsPage.quality: Mappings are documented. Failures retry and surface. Secrets stay out of the workflow. If a sync breaks on a Friday, someone should see why without opening five admin panels.
integrationsPage.delivery: Assessment of the current tools and the first workflow worth connecting, a production integration with monitoring, then the next slice.

faq.q: Can you work with the tools we already bought?
faq.a: That is the point. We integrate what you already pay for unless a tool is genuinely the blocker.

faq.q: Is this the same as AI Agents?
faq.a: No. This is connections and process modernization. An agent that uses those connections to do work is the AI Agents offering.
Not as a first move. We replace the painful workflow around it. A rip-and-replace is a different, explicit decision.

integrationsPage.ctaTitle: Tired of the same record in three systems?
integrationsPage.ctaBody: Tell us the tools, the field that never matches and the failure you cannot afford. We will tell you if an integration is the right first slice.

trengie.title: Trengie: railway engineering website
trengie.summary: Ashen designed and built the public website for Trengie, a railway engineering and consulting firm that presents signaling, electrification, telecommunications, rolling stock and project management services.
trengie.challenge: Trengie needed a credible digital presence for institutional and corporate buyers. The company works across signaling, electrification, telecommunications, rolling stock and technical project consulting: a dense B2B offering that had to stay clear on mobile and desktop.
trengie.built: Ashen delivered the production marketing website at trengie.com: service modules, project portfolio storytelling, standards-focused positioning (ISO, CENELEC, RAMS/SIL4, PMI/IPMA) and a contact path for institutional inquiries.
trengie.approach: The site is structured around how a technical buyer evaluates a railway consultant: capabilities first, then project evidence, then a direct request for consulting. Layout, typography and responsive behavior were designed so long technical descriptions remain readable on phones without hiding the commercial CTA.
trengie.outcome: Trengie has a live Spanish-language public website that presents a complex engineering practice as a coherent commercial offer.
